risks: A validating manifest is a declared-shape verdict, not proof of execution: it never opens the qrels/runfile/result files, never checks a sha256 against contents, and never calls a provider. Trusting the numbers requires actually running the pipeline on a real ready_real dataset.
Placeholder-hash detection is a small denylist (PLACEHOLDER/TODO/TBD); an arbitrary fake-but-non-denylisted hash string would pass the shape check (it still cannot be verified against a file here).
Metric presence/type is enforced but value ranges (beyond latency ordering) are not; a manifest could declare implausible metric values and still pass shape validation.
The contract mirrors the playbook metric set; if that set changes, both should be updated together.
